description: Decentralized AI-driven coordination tools, initially used for strike logistics in France and Belgium, evolve into a transnational network of algorithmic labor organizers. These systems autonomously identify vulnerable sectors, draft legal complaints, and schedule actions across jurisdictions, blurring the line between human-led protest and AI-initiated civil disruption. The phenomenon gains attention after a coordinated wave of public-sector walkouts linked by identical timing patterns and messaging structures.
